purpose: Canonical empirical owner for African regional integration systems and status history. REC membership does not imply North/West/East/South orientation.

african-union.label: African Union
non_canonical_members: Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic / Western Sahara

ecowas.label: Economic Community of West African States

comesa.label: Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa

eccas.label: Economic Community of Central African States

EGY.note: Egypt is a U.S. Major Non-NATO Ally while also retaining its existing East/BRICS overlap and North African/Middle Eastern junction role.

NGA.note: Nigeria is a BRICS partner country, creating an East-facing bridge without overriding its primary West African/ECOWAS regional context.

UGA.note: Uganda is a BRICS partner country, creating an East-facing bridge while EAC remains its stronger regional institutional context.

MAR.note: Morocco has a dense Euro-Mediterranean/EU strategic partnership that makes it a strong North-facing bridge without making it North-primary.
Morocco is also a U.S. Major Non-NATO Ally.

TUN.note: Tunisia is a Euro-Mediterranean North African bridge rather than a North-primary state.
Tunisia is a U.S. Major Non-NATO Ally.

DZA.note: Algeria belongs to the Mediterranean/North African interface but retains sufficient strategic autonomy that frontier is safer than ordinary North membership.

KEN.note: Kenya is a U.S. Major Non-NATO Ally; EAC remains its stronger African regional context.

TZA.note: Tanzania participates in the Southern African system through SADC while simultaneously belonging to EAC; the overlap is intentional.

AGO.note: Angola is a substantial SADC/Southern African node; this does not imply subordination to South Africa.

axis_rule: Axis overlays are selective interpretive/empirical correspondences and are never inferred automatically from REC membership. Countries absent from axis_overlays remain unchanged/unresolved unless classified by the separate world-axis-profiles owner.
